clue.text: Thick-necked type of stereotypical Englishman: John Terry, only more so?

parts.note: John Bull is the cartoon figure who personifies England, so his surname is used here
the footballer's surname treated as an adjective and given a comparative ending, as happy becomes happier

explanation.surface: A burly footballer, John Terry, is pictured as the archetypal beefy Englishman, only more so.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bull is the traditional personification of England, like Uncle Sam for the US. John Terry is a former England football captain; 'only more so' turns Terry into a mock comparative, the way -er makes happier from happy.
explanation.definitionFit: This dog breed is famous for its muscular build and short thick neck, so it is fairly described as a thick-necked type.

clue.text: Guide drug seller quietly away

indicators.note: the quiet letter is sent away, so it is taken out of the dealer word

parts.note: a pusher sells illegal drugs
P stands for piano, the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: Someone shows a drug dealer out of the building without fuss.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who shows people to their seats in a theatre or church guides them, so the noun matches guide.

clue.text: Hide, anticipating Spooner asking "What time do you call this?"

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so his version of the question is used

parts.note: the opening of the scolding question asks why someone is coming in
the end of the question complains that the arrival is late

explanation.surface: Someone lurks in hiding, ready to scold a latecomer with the classic angry question.
explanation.walkthrough: The question is paraphrased as WHY IN LATE; swapping the W and L sounds gives LIE IN WAIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To lie in wait is to conceal yourself while expecting someone to arrive, which is hiding in anticipation.

clue.text: Check whether that is right, son — they swear it is so

parts.note: to test something is to check it
if can mean whether, as in 'see if it works'
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
S is the genealogical abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A fact-checker asks whether something is correct, while a son insists it is true.
explanation.definitionFit: People giving evidence under oath declare that their account is true, which is swearing that something is so.

clue.text: See 1
Charlie knocks out 26 in puffed-up food fight

indicators.note: one letter knocks the other out of its place, taking its spot in the dish

parts.note: a souffle is a light dish that rises in the oven
the answer to 26 down is the NATO alphabet word for O
Charlie is the NATO alphabet word for C

explanation.surface: A food fight breaks out with a souffle as the weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 26 down, the radio code word for the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A confused, disorderly struggle at close quarters is a brief fight or tussle.

clue.text: Warm enough to navigate fierce English rips

indicators.note: the letters are torn apart and reassembled, as something ripped up

explanation.surface: Fierce English currents tear through waters that are warm enough to sail.
explanation.definitionFit: Water with no frozen surface can be sailed, which happens when the climate is mild enough to keep it from freezing.

clue.text: Perhaps Murdoch and Heaney, primarily, were this?

definitions.text: Perhaps Murdoch and Heaney, primarily, were this?

parts.note: Iris Murdoch, the novelist, is one example of the first name

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter of the poet's name is used

explanation.surface: A literary quiz question about the nationality of a novelist and a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: Iris Murdoch was born in Dublin and Seamus Heaney in Northern Ireland, so the whole clue also defines the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both writers were born on the island of Ireland, so the nationality adjective describes them both.

clue.text: Told the authorities about Liberal speech, informally

indicators.note: the confession word goes around the party letter

parts.note: to sing or have sung is ... for informing to the police

explanation.surface: Someone reported a Liberal politician's casual remarks to the authorities.
explanation.definitionFit: Very informal vocabulary used in casual talk rather than standard language is a kind of informal speech.

clue.text: Surreal Greek humour beginning to upset departing tyrannical regime

indicators.note: surreal humour is bizarre and jumbled, signalling the letters are rearranged
the opening letter of the next word leaves the pool of letters
only the first letter of the following word is wanted

explanation.surface: Odd Greek jokes manage to offend a brutal government as it leaves power.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange GREEK HUMOUR after the U from the start of 'upset' has gone out of it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cambodian communist movement that ruled from 1975 to 1979 was notorious for mass killings, a tyrannical regime.

clue.text: One of fifty women entertained by this clue

indicators.note: being entertained by someone means being taken in, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: this clue is 10 across, written as IO and A

explanation.surface: A woman is the guest of honour of fifty, entertained by the clue itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This clue' is 10-across: 10 looks like the letters I and O, and A stands for across.
explanation.definitionFit: This Midwest US state is one of the fifty states of the union.

clue.text: Wife of former President tours European nation

indicators.note: the wife goes round the letter, as a tourist circles a country

parts.note: Carla Bruni is married to Nicolas Sarkozy, a former French president

explanation.surface: A former first lady goes on a tour of a European nation.
explanation.definitionFit: This small sultanate on the island of Borneo is an independent country.

clue.text: 1/4d is distant object

parts.note: far means a long way off, distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A coin's value is stated like a fact, then likened to something far away.
explanation.walkthrough: In pre-decimal British money d stood for a penny, and a quarter-penny coin was worth 1/4d.
explanation.definitionFit: The old British coin worth a quarter of a penny had this name until it was withdrawn in 1960.

clue.text: Bread extremely chewy in French city

parts.note: naan, also spelt nan, is a flat bread

indicators.note: at the extremes means the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A food critic complains that the bread in a French city is very chewy.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Lorraine in north-eastern France is a city famous for Art Nouveau.

clue.text: Military commander is horrified, losing good man

indicators.note: the horrified word loses the saint, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: aghast means filled with horror
ST, for saint, is a crossword stock for a good man

explanation.surface: A general is appalled at losing one of his best soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Ottoman Empire the title was given to military officers and commanders.

clue.text: Old American quits? Lovely stuff

indicators.note: the old American leaves, so those letters are removed from the lovely word

parts.note: gorgeous means very beautiful or lovely
US is short for the United States, hence American

explanation.surface: An old American gives up something, then calls something else lovely stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat greedily, which matches the verb meaning to eat to excess.

clue.text: Choosing again, thinking Earl must replace female

indicators.note: one letter has to take the place of the other within the thinking word

parts.note: reflecting means thinking deeply

explanation.surface: Someone reconsidering a vote decides an Earl should take over from a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Voting the same person back into office is choosing them for a second time.

clue.text: Religion — it's endless for one country's leader

indicators.note: the religion loses its final letter

parts.note: Taoism is the Chinese philosophy and religion
each means for one, as in a pound each

explanation.surface: A pronouncement that a faith goes on forever, for one nation's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the title of the Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: The Irish word for chieftain is the official title of the head of the government of Ireland.

clue.text: I'm chattier performing sums?

indicators.note: the letters perform, putting on a different arrangement as actors do

explanation.surface: Someone becomes more talkative while working out calculations.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing sums with numbers is basic calculation, the plain school subject of number work.

clue.text: Mock butler whimsically in conversation?

indicators.note: spoken in conversation, words are judged by their sound rather than spelling

parts.note: jokingly a butler is a male housemaid, a man maid

explanation.surface: Someone teases a butler with a playful remark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a verb about teasing the butler, but it is an adjective here.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock as an adjective means imitation or artificial, the sense of a fabric not found in nature.

clue.text: Time to struggle with shed's supporting structure

indicators.note: the struggle word has shed the letter, casting it off

parts.note: to wrestle is to struggle

explanation.surface: It is time to tackle the shed's wobbly support.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of a beam on splayed legs supports a table top, so it is a supporting structure.

clue.text: Most senior ministers throw out probes about alien visitor

indicators.note: one piece pokes into the other, as a probe goes inside

parts.note: CA, for circa, means about
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial visitor
to bin something is to throw it out

explanation.surface: Someone discards spacecraft probes sent to study an alien.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior ministers who head government departments form the governing committee.

clue.text: Stone attached to axes

parts.note: on means fixed to, as a lid on a jar
y and x are the two axes of a graph

explanation.surface: A stone is tied to some axes, perhaps as a whetstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axes' suggests chopping tools, but it means the x and y axes of a graph.
explanation.definitionFit: This banded variety of chalcedony is a semi-precious gemstone.

clue.text: Condemn piece of prose

definitions.meaning: a judge condemns a criminal by passing judgement on them
a grammatical unit of words with a subject and verb

explanation.surface: A critic condemns a bit of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge passes punishment on a convict, and a grammar unit ending in a full stop shares the same word.

clue.text: Keeps ignoring piece of tatty clothing

indicators.note: ignoring a letter means leaving it out of the word

parts.note: a shop that stocks goods keeps them for sale

indicators.note: only a small piece of the word is taken, its first letter

explanation.surface: A wardrobe keeper refuses to throw out any scrap of shabby clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Short knitted coverings for the feet are items of clothing.

clue.text: Treatise followed on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard and not seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: to have tracked someone is to have followed them

explanation.surface: An essay that was serialised on a radio programme.
explanation.definitionFit: A pamphlet or short written work on a religious or political subject is a treatise.

clue.text: Type of 1/4d is godsend getting across street

indicators.note: the godsend spans across the street abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a boon is a godsend, a welcome blessing

explanation.surface: An old coin turns out to be a godsend for crossing the street.
explanation.walkthrough: '1/4d' looks like the coin in 12 across, but here it means 1-across/4-down, the dog breed.
explanation.definitionFit: The small American dog breed descends from bull and terrier crosses, so it is a type of the larger breed.

clue.text: Gong found in limousine?

parts.note: a limousine is a very long car; read the answer split, outsize (OS) plus car, and it describes one

explanation.surface: A film star leaves an award in the back of a limousine.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: OS is the clothing-size abbreviation for outsize, and an outsize car is a fair description of a limousine.
explanation.definitionFit: Gong is British slang for a medal or award, and the Academy Award statuette is the film world's best-known one.

clue.text: Firm agreement in Moscow for concluding passage

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm
da is Russian for yes

explanation.surface: A company deal in Moscow forms the closing part of a business story.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the final section that rounds off a movement is its concluding passage.

clue.text: Instruction in well regulated disco for audience

parts.note: a well-run event gives timed instructions, such as do this at ten
a disco is a dance

explanation.surface: Instructions posted at a tightly run disco, for the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an order at a strictly run party: 'At ten, dance'.
explanation.definitionFit: The people present at an event, counted together, make up the crowd or audience.

clue.text: Resolution of dispute in village?

definitions.meaning: an agreement that ends a quarrel or a legal case
a small community where people have made homes

explanation.surface: A dispute in a village is resolved.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreed end to a legal case shares its name with a place where people have put down roots.

clue.text: Two brothers together protect Rosemary, perhaps

indicators.note: the doubled word protects the answer by wrapping it, so the letters on either side are stripped away
two copies of the sibling word are written side by side
the two copies are run together with no gap between them

parts.note: the plural asks for the word for a male sibling

explanation.surface: Two brothers band together to look after their sister Rosemary.
explanation.walkthrough: Write 'brother' twice with no gap and the answer sits across the join, guarded by BROT on one side and ROTHER on the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosemary is an aromatic plant used in cooking, an example of a culinary plant of that kind.
